gaps.sentence: The concert tickets sold ___ within an hour.
gaps.explanation: sell out = all tickets/goods are sold.

gaps.sentence: I can't put up ___ this noise any longer.
I had to turn ___ their invitation because I was ill.
gaps.explanation: turn down = reject an offer/invitation; turn up = appear.

gaps.sentence: Do you get ___ well with your new colleagues?
gaps.explanation: get on (with) = have a good relationship; also get along with (AmE).

gaps.sentence: I'm really looking forward to ___ you again soon.
gaps.explanation: look forward TO + -ing: 'to' is a preposition here.

gaps.sentence: The team was let ___ by its own supporters.
gaps.explanation: let somebody down = disappoint them by failing to help.

gaps.sentence: The bonus made up ___ all the overtime we had done.
gaps.explanation: make up FOR something = compensate for it.

gaps.sentence: They've just moved ___ to their new flat.
gaps.explanation: move in = start living in a new home.
